page: Amazon Web Services mac-m3ultra.metal is a bare-metal macOS instance powered by dedicated Apple silicon hardware. Built on the arm64_mac architecture, the server provides 28 physical CPU cores operating at a base frequency of 4.0 GHz with a single thread per core. Memory allocation is dense, offering 256.0 GB of system memory, which translates to approximately 9.14 GB per physical core. The instance includes a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile and does not contain integrated hardware GPUs or local storage.

Because the server lacks local NVMe storage, persistent storage and operating disk requirements must be provisioned through network-attached block storage volumes. This design trades local disk throughput for operational flexibility in lifecycle management. The hardware provides dedicated physical execution without virtualization overhead, ensuring deterministic compute cycles and consistent execution latency across all 28 cores. Cost efficiency is driven by the high compute density and extensive memory footprint, allowing consolidation of multiple concurrent build or test pipelines onto a single physical node.

Workload applicability centers on enterprise macOS build environments, continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipelines, multi-platform software compilation, and large Xcode test suites. The extensive 256.0 GB memory capacity also accommodates memory-intensive macOS-native applications, large simulator instances, and native multimedia processing pipelines that require high per-core RAM capacity.
description: Amazon Web Services mac-m3ultra.metal is a dedicated bare-metal macOS server designed for compute and memory-intensive Apple ecosystem operations. Built on the arm64_mac architecture, it features 28 physical Apple CPU cores clocked at 4.0 GHz with one thread per core, accompanied by 256.0 GB of memory for an allocation of 9.14 GB per core. The instance provides 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operates without dedicated GPUs, and does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for disk operations. Eliminating hypervisor overhead guarantees fully deterministic processor utilization. The server delivers cost efficiency through resource consolidation, making it practical to execute multiple resource-heavy compilation jobs simultaneously. mac-m3ultra.metal is well matched for enterprise continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines, Xcode application builds, multi-target testing suites, and data-heavy macOS-native processing workloads.
